description: Public keys that verify Trinity authority receipts. Append-only: an entry is never removed or rewritten, because receipts signed under a retired or compromised key must remain verifiable forever.

statuses.example: Demonstrates the schema. Never signed anything. Never a trust root.
statuses.retired: No longer signing. Receipts it signed remain valid; verify them normally.
statuses.compromised: The private key is believed exposed. Signatures still verify cryptographically, so a verifier reports a DISTINCT verdict rather than pass or fail — see the verifier's own output for what that verdict can and cannot establish.

entries.note: SCHEMA EXAMPLE ONLY. Deterministically generated from a published string so anyone can reproduce it and confirm it is not a secret. Its validity window is closed and its status is `example`; no verifier will accept it as a trust root. It exists so the format is demonstrated before a production key is generated, and it is replaced by entry one when it is.

The first production signing key. Generated by the operator, held as PROOF_RECEIPT_SIGNING_KEY and never present in this repository or its history. The fingerprint here is pinned independently in CorePolicy's receipt_signing_policy, so a receipt signed under a key this registry does not name is a named integrity finding rather than a silent pass. `valid_to` is null because the key is currently signing; it is set when the key retires, and the entry is never removed.
